summary: Adversary r3 FAIL on plan rev 3 dbc93551 (delta 567d70ac..dbc93551: B12-outreach-plan.md, B12-outreach-plan-cells.md, template rule 24 b72c8976). Code reference origin/main 99266f52. Prior r2: 16 FIXED (ADV-2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 20, 22, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 32, 33, 34, 35), 6 PARTIALLY_FIXED (ADV-4, 8, 23, 24, 26, 31). New: 0 BLOCKING, 5 MAJOR (ADV-36..40), 5 MINOR (ADV-41..45). Checked against code and found true: seller S at commercial-sales.ts:339 and CMD050 row FOR NO KEY UPDATE :369 then X :372, so the seller readers take no row lock and there is no access/CMD050 cycle; owner subject :857; unassignProspects UPDATE :618 does not change state; transition_key is a bigint hashtextextended (0001:267-269), so a pg_locks held-lock assertion is feasible; claim_lease takes the lease row FOR UPDATE then judges GREATEST(p_now, effect_now()) (0067:20-22); holdDispatchLease judges a caller instant (commission-service-access.ts:172), so the new holdOutreachLease is needed; server.ts:504-505 parses every body as bytes and admission.ts:115 is the JSON gate, so a per-route RFC 8058 admission is possible. Global order: no cycle. Every trace in plan section 2 is a subsequence of L1, L2, L3, L4, L4g, L5, L6, L6p, L7, L8, L10, L11, L12, L13, L14; D4 now takes L4/L4g before L7 (ADV-22 closed); revoke (L4g X) and withdraw (L6p X) hold nothing after their subject; X holders of L8 take one key, so the two-key S holders cannot cycle; the CMD045 trigger (0029:991-1005) is BEFORE INSERT and CMD045 holds only L1 S and L2 before it, so acquiring L8 S there is order-safe (but contradicts the plan sentence, ADV-44). 'Triggers only assert (KA096 LOCK_NOT_HELD)' is sound for the outreach tables, provided the per-edge table of ADV-42 exists; direct INSERT paths in fixtures pass through the same triggers. Calendar facts verified: Colombian holidays (holidays.ts:93-142, Ley 51/1983 + Ley 2578/2026) give 2027-01-11, 2027-07-05 and 2027-07-12 (July 9 moved to Monday); 2027-07-13 is a business day in both zones; US observed days 2026-07-03, 2027-06-18, 2027-07-05, 2027-12-24, 2027-12-31, 2028-11-10 are right (5 U.S.C. 6103(b)(1) Saturday->Friday, E.O. 11582 Sunday->Monday). Dropped cells: GAP-OO-2 (the opt-out locks the one contact key of its token) and GAP-SE-9/GAP-SE-13 (rev 2 sweep pairs, 60b693e0:115-116; rev 3 has no sweep) are dropped for true reasons; section 8 r1 rows still cite them (ADV-44). D-33: no ranking, segment or buyer-type rule in rev 3; new tables are Kauro's own; no CRM write path. Rejected because the reachability family recurs a third round: the L12 intent lock serializes every L10 pair, so M26-M29 and M41 stay green with the named lock removed (ADV-36); M22 / R2-130 (same prospect) uses a token that cannot exist before the claim (ADV-37); a same-fence late answer onto OBSERVED_NOT_SENT is dropped and the HUMAN NOT_SENT bound does not cover the call (ADV-38); the opt-out GET page cannot pass the JSON-only reply guard (ADV-39); KA098(b) is refused by two guards (ADV-40). Own correction of r2: r2 called GAP-SUP-1 reachable with two actors; true only when CMD045 passes its app pre-checks (register-prospect.ts:66-70) before the prospect is born (ADV-41). Root cause required before round 4 (CLAUDE.md rule 5): amend template rule 24 (see template_rule_needed). Family-coverage table waits for the PASS round.

findings.title: Rule-24 controls masked by a later conflicting lock: every L10 pair also takes L12 FOR NO KEY UPDATE before its judgment, so M26, M27, M28, M29 and M41 stay green with the named lock (or UNIQUE) removed
findings.reproduction: Traces: D4 and D4b take L10 -> L12 (plan:232-233); D5 takes L10, L12, L13 (plan:235); CMD064 HUMAN takes L10 -> L12 (plan:246-247); every judgment follows the last lock. M26 (D4b x D5), M27 (D4 x D5), M28 (HUMAN x D4b) and M29 (HUMAN x HUMAN) name L10 with 'Also L12' and control kind (b): the L10 locking read made plain. With only that change both actors still wait at the intent row FOR NO KEY UPDATE (L12) before the judgment; the second re-reads the first's committed state and returns the same clean outcome, so the cell stays green. M41 (D4 x D4 redelivery, control (c) UNIQUE dropped) also stays green: L10/L12 serialize the two D4s and the existence check ('if this intent's activity of that kind exists: no-op', plan:233) sees the first activity. The done criterion (plan:299-300, every section-M cell red under its listed control) cannot be met for five rows; under rule 24 such a cell is not C. Related: M35 control (c) goes red only because INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key_kind, suppression_key) has no arbiter once the UNIQUE is dropped (42P10, even sequentially), not because of a duplicate.
findings.acceptance_criterion: For each pair the serializer is the full set of conflicting locks taken before the judgment (here {L10, L12}): the control removes the whole set, or the plan drops the redundant lock, or each lock is shown necessary by its own cell. M41 names the guard under test (existence check under L10/L12, or the UNIQUE with the locks removed). M35's control makes a real duplicate possible or is relabelled a static guard. Template rule 24 amended (template_rule_needed).

findings.title: M22 / R2-130 (same prospect) is self-fulfilling: the opt-out uses the queued follow-up's own token, which exists only in the MIME D3 sends after D2 COMMIT, so order 1 cannot happen and order 2 is sequential
findings.reproduction: Token = HMAC(secret v, intent id) (plan:254), carried in that intent's List-Unsubscribe and body (A13, plan:86-87). A QUEUED follow-up has never been submitted; D2 commits SUBMITTING before D3 (plan:231) and every refusal sends nothing, so no recipient holds that token until after D2 commits. Order 1 ('opt-out first: NOT_SENT(SUPPRESSED), zero calls') needs a token the recipient cannot have (the test would compute it from the intent id); order 2 cannot overlap D2's L8 hold. The reachable interleaving, which is what R2-130 describes ('A recipient opts out after grant creation and before dispatcher claim'), is an opt-out through the FIRST message's token while the follow-up is QUEUED: same meeting point (L8; the opt-out takes no L3/L4/L4g/L10/L12), KEY SHARE only on the first intent's row.
findings.acceptance_criterion: R2-130 (same prospect) and M22 use the token of an already submitted message of the same contact and prospect, with both orders and the L8-removed control; the test support refuses to build an opt-out request from the token of an intent that was never submitted.
findings.failing_test: b12-dispatch-cells :: 'R2-130 (same prospect): opt-out through the first message's token against the claim of the queued follow-up, held at L8: order 1 NOT_SENT(SUPPRESSED) zero calls; order 2 one submission then SUPPRESSED; red with D2's L8 removed'.

findings.title: Late answers, sweep of ADV-24: a same-fence D4 that finds the intent OBSERVED_NOT_SENT is refused by KA096 and its answer is dropped (D4b runs only on LEASE_FENCED); the HUMAN NOT_SENT bound submitted_at + callBound (DB clock, stamped before COMMIT) does not cover D3's abort (app clock, from the call start after COMMIT)
findings.reproduction: D2 stamps submitted_at = effect_now inside the claim unit (plan:231). D3 starts after COMMIT and aborts callBound after its own start (plan:32-33), so the call can still be live up to (commit latency + scheduling) past submitted_at + callBound; D4 can also wait at L3/L4, time out and retry (GAP-DI-8). HUMAN_SEND_OBSERVED NOT_SENT is admitted at or after submitted_at + callBound when no accepted answer or evidence row exists (plan:35). Sequence: D2 commits at T; D3 starts at T+d; the human records NOT_SENT at submitted_at + callBound (intent OBSERVED_NOT_SENT, draft DRAFT); a repeat CMD063 is queued; the provider accepts the first call before T+d+callBound; the same owner's D4 (fence unchanged: no LEASE_FENCED, no D4b) tries the edge OBSERVED_NOT_SENT to PROVIDER_ACCEPTED, which KA096 refuses (every edge out of NOT_SENT, CANCELLED and the OBSERVED states, plan:235; cells:31 (e)). The unit rolls back: the answer is lost, no evidence row exists, the repeat's claim does not see NOT_SENT(ALREADY_SENT), and the contact receives the message twice. A3 'never drops the answer' (plan:36) holds only for the fenced path; M28 covers only D4b, GAP-DI-7b only SEND_UNCERTAIN. Analogous paths that drop a received answer (conservative, leaving SEND_UNCERTAIN): GAP-DI-8 (D4 commit timeout) and GAP-DI-9 (activity INSERT failure).
findings.acceptance_criterion: (1) Any D4 whose intent is not in an edge-admissible state (OBSERVED_NOT_SENT, OBSERVED_SENT, PROVIDER_ACCEPTED with another ref) takes the D4b evidence path regardless of the fence. (2) The HUMAN NOT_SENT and D5 bounds cover the call's real lifetime: D3 derives its abort from the DB instant (submitted_at + callBound minus effect_now read just before the call; NOT_ATTEMPTED if not positive), or the bound adds a stated start slack that D3 enforces. (3) GAP-DI-8/GAP-DI-9 state whether the answer is retried into D4b or only left SEND_UNCERTAIN, listed as a caveat.
findings.failing_test: b12-dispatch-cells :: 'GAP-DI-23 (same fence, after HUMAN NOT_SENT): provider accepts after the human's NOT_SENT; the same owner's D4 writes an evidence row, intent stays OBSERVED_NOT_SENT, the repeat's claim is NOT_SENT(ALREADY_SENT) with zero calls' (red today: KA096 rollback, repeat submitted) + 'EXPIRY (call start): D3 started past the claim + slack is NOT_ATTEMPTED; HUMAN NOT_SENT never admitted while the fake holds an open call'.

findings.title: Sweep of ADV-26, reply side: the opt-out GET confirmation page (HTML) cannot be sent, because the API onSend guard refuses every reply that is not a JSON object body; the file that would change (server.ts) is in the API-REG set, not owned by L-ACT
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/server.ts:399-415 (99266f52): onSend refuses any payload that is not a checked JSON object (ResponseContractViolation 'not a JSON object body'); onRoute (server.ts:351-357) refuses a route without a response contract. The plan has 'GET renders a confirmation page whose form POSTs the same body to the same URL (RFC 8058 s.3.2) and writes nothing' (plan:262-263) and OPT-OUT DENY (GET) (plan:269). The message's body link is the opt-out that works even when DKIM does not cover the headers (plan:327); a human who clicks it receives the guard's problem reply instead of a page. Section 3 gives server.ts to the API-REG set (plan:282); L-ACT owns only opt-out-route.ts (plan:293). The POST 200 JSON reply is fine.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The plan decides where the human page lives: either the web app serves a public page that POSTs the RFC form body to the API route, or the API gets a declared text/html reply contract for exactly this route, the guard change owned by a named lane, with a cell showing every other route still refuses a non-JSON reply. The OPT-OUT GET cell runs through the real HTTP server and asserts content type and form target.

findings.title: Sweep of ADV-31: KA098 (b) is refused by two guards (KA098 itself requires target state SUPPRESSED, plan:314, cells:26, and so does the policy WITH CHECK), so dropping either alone leaves (b) refused; the staging that makes (a) and (d) single-guard is not stated
findings.reproduction: D-B12O-12 (plan:314): 'KA098 guard: a non-owner prospect UPDATE changes only state/suppressed/version/updated_at, to SUPPRESSED, with a matching suppression row'; cells:26 says the same. KA098 (b) is 'a seller UPDATE of its own prospect to CONTACTED (KA098 admits state; only the policy WITH CHECK state = SUPPRESSED refuses)'. KA098 does not admit it: CONTACTED is not SUPPRESSED. With the WITH CHECK dropped, KA098 still refuses (b): the control stays green, breaking rule 12 (each control red alone with its guard dropped). findings.title: Whole-lane sweep (rule 14, outside the delta): L5, L6 and L7 are row FOR SHARE locks, which 0001:258-265 (N3) avoids for facts whose writers suspend or revoke, because overlapping share lockers starve the waiting FOR NO KEY UPDATE writer; platform capability readers use the advisory subject instead
findings.reproduction: 0001:258-265: a share lock is granted beside current share lockers even while an UPDATE waits, so a stream of overlapping commands could starve a suspension, restriction or revocation (N3); readers therefore take no row lock on those rows. Capability readers on main use awaitTransition('kauro.capabilities', mode) (commerce-subject.ts:68, workspace.ts:598). B12 reads capability rows (L5), resource rows (L6) and sender rows (L7) FOR SHARE against CMD059 SUSPENDED, publisher SUPERSEDED and RecordSenderRevocation. Rule 16 allows FOR SHARE and outreach volume is low, so this is liveness, not safety; but the platform protocol and the plan's own L4g/L6p advisory choice point the other way.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Either the revocation-class facts (L5, L7, L6 for supersession) use advisory subjects with the writer's X, like L4g/L6p, or the plan records why row share locks are acceptable (bounded unit length, volume) with a TIMEOUT cell for the writer.
